Turn every image into an edge map.

Canny gives white edges on black; Sobel, Laplacian and Scharr give the edge strength. Sobel and Scharr can give one direction (x: left-right changes, y: top-bottom) or the gradient's angle. LoG smooths with sigma before the Laplacian; DoG is the difference of two blurs (sigma, sigma 2). Colour images are made grey first, so the output has one channel and the model's input becomes [H, W, 1]. Done once when the images are prepared: OpenCV on the CPU workers, in canvas order with the other steps done once; every epoch reads the result. Same result in training, validation and test.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Method | `method` | Choice | `canny` | `canny`, `sobel`, `laplacian`, `scharr`, `log`, `dog` | The run | Edge detector. |
| Direction | `direction` | Choice | `magnitude` | `magnitude`, `x`, `y`, `angle` | The run | Sobel and Scharr: both directions' size, one direction, or the angle. |
| Low threshold | `threshold1` | Number | `50` | `>=0` | The run | Canny: weak edge threshold (0 to 255 scale) |
| High threshold | `threshold2` | Number | `150` | `>=0` | The run | Canny: strong edge threshold, at least the low one. |
| Kernel size | `kernel_size` | Integer | `3` | `>0` | The run | Sobel: 1, 3, 5 or 7; Laplacian and LoG: odd up to 31; not used by Canny, Scharr and DoG. |
| Sigma | `sigma` | Number | `1.0` | `>0` | The run | LoG: the smoothing before the Laplacian; DoG: the finer blur, in pixels. |
| Sigma 2 | `sigma2` | Number | `1.6` | `>0` | The run | DoG: the coarser blur, greater than sigma. |
| Keep image | `keep_image` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keep the image and add the edge map as one more channel (RGB + edges: 4 channels) |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Usage

```text
Resize -> Image Edges -> Normalize -> Conv2D
```

```text
Done once when the images are prepared (OpenCV, CPU), in canvas order before the first random step. Runs in training, validation and test.
```

## Tips

- Shapes matter more than colour or texture.
- The model's input becomes [H, W, 1], or [H, W, C + 1] with Keep image.

## Methods and directions

Colour images are made grey first.

| `method` | What it computes | Settings it reads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canny` | thin white edges on black (two thresholds, 0 to 255 scale) | `threshold1`, `threshold2` |
| `sobel` | the first derivative, smoothed | `kernel_size` (1, 3, 5 or 7), `direction` |
| `scharr` | the same with a more accurate 3 x 3 kernel | `direction` |
| `laplacian` | the second derivative: answers to any direction, and to noise | `kernel_size` |
| `log` | Laplacian of Gaussian: a blur of `sigma` first, so it answers to edges of that scale and not to noise | `sigma`, `kernel_size` |
| `dog` | Difference of Gaussians: blur `sigma` minus blur `sigma2`, the detail between the two scales (close to LoG when `sigma2` is 1.6 x `sigma`) | `sigma`, `sigma2` (greater than `sigma`) |

`direction` (Sobel and Scharr):

- `magnitude`: the mean of both directions' sizes, 0.5 |gx| + 0.5 |gy|.
- `x`: |gx|, changes from left to right, so vertical edges light up.
- `y`: |gy|, changes from top to bottom, so horizontal edges light up.
- `angle`: the gradient's direction, 0 to 360 degrees stored as 0 to 255. 0
  is brighter to the right, 64 brighter downwards, 128 brighter to the
  left, 191 brighter upwards; flat areas are 0. The value wraps (255 is next
  to 0), so it suits looking at more than feeding a model.

Strengths are stored as their size, cut at 255.

**Keep image** (`keep_image`) keeps the image and adds the edge map as one
more channel: an RGB image becomes 4 channels (R, G, B, edges), a grey one
2, and the model's first layer reads `[H, W, 4]`. See
[More than three channels](../categories/preprocessing.md#more-than-three-channels).

```text
Data Input (images) -> Resize 72 -> Image Edges (canny, keep image)
  -> Center Crop 64 -> Normalize (same 0.5 / 0.5) -> Conv2D -> ...
```

`examples/cyxgraph/cats_dogs_edges_channel.cyxgraph` is a small
cats-vs-dogs CNN that reads the photo and its edges.
